corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science records, large language models are studied as cognitive processes, research tools, and social actors. Findings illuminate trust, embodiment, and dependence in human-AI interactions; methodological use of LLMs for coding, measurement, and policy analysis; and applications spanning health communication, education, ESG, and governance. The corpus underscores the need for transparency, equity, and critical evaluation in deploying AI in society.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and user experience
themes.description: A broad set of studies investigates trust, perceived humanness, embodiment, and behavioral responses to AI across health, education, and everyday contexts.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological innovator in social science
themes.description: Researchers deploy LLMs and related tools to assist data collection, coding, evaluation, forecasting, and policy analysis, emphasizing validation, transparency, and governance.

themes.name: AI in health, wellbeing, and health communication
themes.description: Research on AI-related health information, patient education, health communication, and clinical decision support, including safety, equity, and accessibility concerns.

themes.name: AI in education and learning sciences
themes.description: Exploration of AI's role in learning, teaching, assessment, curriculum design, and AI literacy, including teacher training and student engagement.

emergingKeywords: trust and transparency in human-AI interaction
